fixes.explanation: Silent doesn't fit here. Moses says the LORD spoke these commandments "in a loud voice" to the whole assembly (Deuteronomy 5:22). Nobody on that mountain was leaning in, asking God to repeat Himself. The word God uses for Himself in this command is jealous.

YES, baker! God says, "You shall have no other gods before Me." Look at what comes right before it. He reminds them He brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery (Deuteronomy 5:6). So He doesn't open with a rule. He opens with "Remember who just carried you out of there." Then the command. I've been rescued from a place myself, and let me tell you, you don't forget who came and got you.

Trade is a fair-sounding guess, but it's not the word. God says, "You shall not steal." That's about taking what belongs to someone else. Trading is two people agreeing to swap, and nobody gets robbed. I came out of the last bin at a closing bakery with a 25 cent sticker on me, and Mother Miller handed over a quarter. Best 25 cents anybody ever spent, and not a crime in sight!

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The explanation is a flat restatement followed by generic praise. It lacks Papa Dorin's distinctive voice.
The story about being purchased ends with a flat, obvious distinction between paying and stealing, without a laugh or much personality.
